He has not had dialysis and has no trauma history. His only recent procedure was an endovascular repair of an iliac artery performed through the left groin. Which is the most likely cause?
Which electrocardiogram changes occur in Takotsubo (stress) cardiomyopathy?
A 63-year-old man has an incidental 4.0 cm ascending thoracic aortic aneurysm on a chest radiograph and follow-up imaging. He has no symptoms. Which surveillance plan is appropriate?

A 57-year-old man survives an out-of-hospital cardiac arrest from pulseless ventricular tachycardia. After stabilization no reversible cause is found. Which device is most appropriate before discharge?
Why is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug approached with caution in older adults with pericarditis?

A 69-year-old woman being evaluated for endocarditis had a soft systolic murmur documented for 10 years. Today the murmur sounds a little louder. How does this change count under the modified Duke criteria?

A 63-year-old woman is diagnosed with constrictive pericarditis. She had mantle-field radiotherapy for Hodgkin lymphoma 25 years ago and is otherwise well. Which feature of her history most worsens her long-term prognosis?

A 54-year-old woman who started a new antibiotic three days ago faints briefly. Her electrocardiogram before the event showed a markedly prolonged QT. The monitor now shows a wide QRS tachycardia whose peaks rise and fall so that the complexes seem to twist around the baseline. Which is the most likely diagnosis?

A 6-year-old with repaired congenital heart disease has 3 weeks of low-grade fever, fatigue, joint aches and weight loss. A new murmur is heard. Which organism most commonly causes endocarditis in this age group?

D.q: A 74-year-old woman with recurrent urinary tract infections was treated for pyelonephritis a month ago. She now has low-grade fevers, fatigue and a new murmur, and blood cultures grow gram-positive cocci. Which organism is most likely?

A 74-year-old man with advanced dilated cardiomyopathy has refractory symptoms on full medical therapy. Severe lung disease and frailty rule him out as a transplant candidate, and he wants to remain at home and mobile. Which treatment option fits his situation?

A 19-year-old swimmer has an electrocardiogram before a sports physical. She has no symptoms. The rate is 72, with a normal P wave before every narrow QRS, but the beats come closer together as she breathes in and spread apart as she breathes out. Which is the most likely diagnosis?
Which medication is a recognized cause of pericardial effusion?
Stable atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response is treated how?
A 69-year-old woman in stable, rate-controlled atrial flutter of unknown duration is to have elective outpatient cardioversion. Which must come first?

A 64-year-old woman has been in the hospital for 2 weeks with a peripherally inserted central line. She develops fever, and two separate blood cultures grow a gram-positive coccus with no other source. Which organism causes the largest share of this setting's native valve endocarditis?
An elevated D-dimer implies increased activity of which process?

A 72-year-old woman had a bioprosthetic aortic valve placed 5 months ago. She now has a fever of 39.0 °C (102.2 °F) and a new regurgitant murmur, and blood cultures have been drawn. Which empiric regimen is most appropriate?
A 70-year-old man has an asymptomatic infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm measuring 3.4 cm on ultrasound. Which follow-up is most appropriate?

A 58-year-old woman received mediastinal radiation and chemotherapy for a chest cancer 15 years ago. She now has progressive exercise intolerance, orthopnea (breathlessness lying flat), ascites and swollen legs. Echocardiogram shows stiff ventricles of normal size, marked atrial enlargement and abnormal diastolic function with a preserved ejection fraction. Which is the most likely diagnosis?

A 40-year-old woman has a regular narrow complex tachycardia at 182 with palpitations and mild anxiety. Her blood pressure is 128/80, oxygen saturation 98%, and she is alert without chest pain. Which treatment should be tried first?

A 74-year-old man with sudden leg ischemia has sensory loss extending beyond the toes with rest pain, mild-to-moderate weakness, an inaudible arterial Doppler signal and an audible venous signal. Where should his evaluation and treatment take place?
A 64-year-old man will finish 5 more weeks of intravenous antibiotics for endocarditis after discharge. Which consultant manages his antibiotic therapy and outpatient monitoring?

A 40-year-old woman has taken ibuprofen and colchicine for 8 days for presumed viral pericarditis. She still has a temperature of 38.5 degrees Celsius and pleuritic (worse with a deep breath) pain, and a new pericardial effusion has appeared on echocardiogram. Which is the most appropriate next step?
When is the dental prophylaxis dose given?
A 44-year-old man arrives with a temperature of 40.2 °C (104.4 °F), rigors and a new murmur, and he looks toxic. Acute endocarditis is suspected. Which is the most appropriate next step?

A 58-year-old man collapses in a gym. He is unresponsive, not breathing and has no pulse. The monitor shows chaotic, irregular waves of varying size with no identifiable QRS complexes. Which rhythm is present?

A 79-year-old man with multiple serious medical conditions is a poor surgical candidate. He had a transient ischemic attack and has a 90% symptomatic carotid stenosis. Which intervention is most appropriate?

A 38-year-old woman notices occasional skipped beats during a stressful month of heavy coffee and wine. Her electrocardiogram shows occasional early beats with an abnormally shaped P wave and a narrow QRS, and her examination and echocardiogram are normal. Which advice is most appropriate?

A 17-year-old basketball player collapses briefly during a game and recovers. In the emergency department he is in sinus rhythm at 78. His electrocardiogram shows a PR interval of 0.10 seconds and a delta wave (a slurred upstroke at the start of the QRS) with a widened QRS. Which is the most likely diagnosis?
Which disorder in the differential of infective endocarditis causes thromboemboli and cardiac valve disease?

A 66-year-old man with a large anterior myocardial infarction two years ago has palpitations and lightheadedness. He is alert, with a blood pressure of 112/70. The monitor shows a regular wide QRS rhythm at 170 per minute with no P waves, every complex the same shape, for over a minute. Which is the most likely diagnosis?

A 71-year-old man admitted with pneumonia develops frequent early, wide QRS beats with no preceding P wave on telemetry, and he feels his heart skipping. His oxygen saturation on the monitor is drifting down. Which is the most appropriate next step?
Which description fits recurrent pericarditis?

A 52-year-old man on telemetry has a prolonged QT after starting a new medication and then develops polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (QRS complexes that vary in shape and twist around the baseline). He becomes unresponsive and pulseless. Which is the most appropriate next step?
What most commonly causes a lower extremity arteriovenous fistula?

A 38-year-old woman has her second recurrence of idiopathic pericarditis despite colchicine. Her temperature is 38.4 degrees Celsius, C-reactive protein is 45 mg/L, and cardiac magnetic resonance shows pericardial edema with late gadolinium enhancement. Which therapy is most appropriate to add?
A 68-year-old man with Mobitz type II block found on a routine tracing declines a pacemaker because he feels perfectly well. Which risk should be explained to him?
Which is the first treatment for torsades de pointes in a conscious patient?

A 74-year-old man with diabetes who smokes wakes most nights with burning pain in his forefoot and toes that eases when he hangs the leg over the bed; he now sleeps in a recliner. Which ankle-brachial index range would be expected?

A 23-year-old previously healthy man has breathlessness, chest pain and exercise intolerance ten days after a flulike illness with fever, myalgia and diarrhea. He is tachycardic with a third heart sound (an early diastolic sound just after the second heart sound) and crackles at both bases. Troponin is elevated and coronary angiography is normal. Which is the most likely diagnosis?

A 49-year-old man has a first proximal deep vein thrombosis with no surgery, trauma, hormone use, travel, cancer or other identifiable trigger, and no inherited disorder has been found. How long should anticoagulation continue?

An 84-year-old woman spent 9 days in the hospital for a large pericardial effusion that needed two procedures. She is now weak and needs help to walk. Besides cardiology and cardiothoracic surgery, which service is most appropriate before she goes home?

D.topic: Differential diagnosis of a swollen leg
D.q: A 57-year-old man with knee osteoarthritis felt a sudden sharp pain behind the right knee while climbing stairs, followed by severe calf discomfort and swelling. Venous duplex ultrasound shows no thrombus. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 27-year-old woman with obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is examined by a student who hears a loud systolic murmur at the left sternal border. Respiration does not change it. Which bedside maneuver would soften her murmur?

A 67-year-old woman is recovering in hospital from stress cardiomyopathy that followed news of her son's serious illness. Her chest pain has resolved, and she asks whether her heart will stay damaged. Which answer about her prognosis is most accurate?

A 68-year-old man who smokes and has diabetes reports aching in both buttocks and hips after walking two blocks, relieved by about 10 minutes of rest. He also reports erectile dysfunction. Both femoral pulses are diminished. Which is the most likely diagnosis?
A 70-year-old woman has a 1.4 cm femoral pseudoaneurysm on ultrasound after cardiac catheterization. She is comfortable and the limb is well perfused. Which management is most appropriate?
What must follow chest or back pain in a patient with a known thoracic aortic aneurysm?
A 51-year-old woman with dilated, tortuous leg veins has a duplex ultrasound confirming superficial venous reflux. Which vein is most commonly involved in this condition?
A 70-year-old man presents with painful blue toes and palpable pedal pulses. On abdominal examination there is a pulsatile mass above the umbilicus. Which lesion is the likely source of his emboli?
In sick sinus syndrome, a fast run that is irregularly irregular with no P waves alternates with pauses. Which rhythm is the fast run?

A 65-year-old woman with a normal pulse examination and ankle-brachial index has had her venous ulcer heal after months of compression. She asks why it opened again after she bumped her leg. Which feature of a healed venous ulcer explains this?

A 76-year-old woman had a mechanical mitral valve placed 4 years ago. She has 5 weeks of low-grade fever and fatigue, and blood cultures are pending. Which organism is most likely in her prosthetic valve infection?

A 58-year-old man receiving chemotherapy for colon cancer comes to the emergency department with three days of left calf swelling that measures 4 cm more than the right, plus tenderness along the deep veins of the calf. He has no history of clots and nothing else explains his leg. The team debates whether to order a D-dimer or go straight to imaging. Using the Wells criteria, which is the best next step?
A 75-year-old man with complete heart block is stabilized with transcutaneous pacing in the emergency department. Which is the definitive treatment?

A 28-year-old man had a cold 10 days ago. He now has sharp, pleuritic (worse with a deep breath) substernal chest pain that is worse lying flat and eases when he leans forward. A pericardial friction rub (a scratchy, squeaking sound) is heard at the left sternal border, and the electrocardiogram shows widespread concave ST elevation with PR depression and ST depression in aVR. Which is the most likely diagnosis?
Where do atherosclerotic lesions most often form?

A 52-year-old man with end-stage dilated cardiomyopathy is listed for cardiac transplantation, but his breathlessness and fatigue worsen despite full medical therapy and a biventricular defibrillator. Which device strategy fits his situation?
A 74-year-old man with heart failure has runs of 5 identical wide QRS beats on a Holter monitor. He has no symptoms during them. Which is the most appropriate management?

A 63-year-old man is diagnosed with a first proximal deep vein thrombosis five days after knee replacement under two hours of general anesthesia. His clot is attributed to the venous stasis and endothelial trauma of the Virchow triad, both from the surgery. What duration of anticoagulation is appropriate?

A 34-year-old woman has been hospitalized for four days receiving intravenous antibiotics through a peripheral catheter in her left forearm. She now has pain, redness and warmth along the course of the vein, and a firm, tender, palpable cord can be felt beneath the skin. She is afebrile, and the redness stays within the line of the vein. Which is the most likely diagnosis?

A 19-year-old college athlete has exertional chest pain without coronary disease and a harsh systolic murmur at the left sternal border. Hypertension and aortic valve disease have been excluded. Which echocardiogram finding confirms the clinical diagnosis of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy?

A 65-year-old woman with lung cancer has a moderate effusion, dyspnea and a blood pressure of 100/68. Her clinician measures her blood pressure through the respiratory cycle. Which result most supports tamponade?

A 2-month-old infant with a central line has poor feeding, fast breathing, tachycardia and a changing murmur. Blood cultures are positive and echocardiography shows a vegetation. Which complications are particularly common in infants because of septic emboli?

Which cardiomyopathy strategy applies specifically to adolescents?

Echocardiogram shows only a small pericardial effusion, estimated at about 150 mL, with right ventricular diastolic collapse. Which best explains why so little fluid has compromised him?

A 68-year-old man is brought in confused, with a blood pressure of 76/40. The monitor shows a slow, regular rhythm at 36 with a normal P wave before every narrow QRS. Which is the first-line treatment?

E.q: When are palliative care discussions raised for elderly patients with cardiomyopathy?
What is the most frequent presumed cause of myocarditis in developed countries?
A 69-year-old man is recovering from a carotid endarterectomy for high-grade symptomatic stenosis. Which complications of the procedure should be monitored for?

A 66-year-old woman with viridans streptococcal endocarditis had positive blood cultures on days 1 and 2 and her first negative culture on day 4. She asks how long her antibiotics will last. Which answer is most accurate?

A 71-year-old woman with restrictive cardiomyopathy has fatigue and exercise intolerance along with leg edema, hepatomegaly and ascites, but her lungs are relatively clear. Which pattern of heart failure is expected to dominate in this condition?

A 62-year-old man with dilated cardiomyopathy and an ejection fraction of 30% is in sinus rhythm, has native heart valves and has no thrombus on echocardiogram. His neighbor with heart failure takes a blood thinner, and he asks whether he should too. Which response about anticoagulation is most accurate?
Which causes should be checked first in a patient with frequent premature ventricular contractions?

A 38-year-old woman has a congenital arteriovenous fistula of the calf with numerous small communications, causing chronic swelling and aching. She has no signs of ischemia or heart failure. Which is the most appropriate initial management?
Acute pericarditis is inflammation of the pericardial sac that lasts less than how long?
A 62-year-old woman with suspected tamponade undergoes right heart catheterization before drainage. Which pressure finding is expected?
Which electrolyte is given as an intravenous push and then as an infusion to break torsades de pointes?
Which description fits a pericardial friction rub?

A 72-year-old man with long-standing hypertension has a routine electrocardiogram. The QRS is 0.16 seconds wide, with a dominant S wave in V1, a broad single-peaked R wave in leads I, V5 and V6, and no Q waves in those leads. Which is the most likely diagnosis?
Which condition is a contraindication to anticoagulation for deep vein thrombosis?

A 33-year-old man had a plaster cast removed from his right lower leg two days ago after a tibial fracture. He now has right calf swelling that measures 4 cm more than the left, and tenderness along the deep veins of the calf. Nothing else on the Wells criteria is present and no alternative diagnosis is as likely. What is his Wells score?

A 26-year-old woman has recurrent atrioventricular nodal reentry episodes that tend to start after coffee, alcohol or decongestant (sympathomimetic) use. She has no heart disease. Which counseling is most appropriate?
A 37-year-old man with acute pericarditis feels better after 5 days of ibuprofen and colchicine and plans to stop both medicines now. Which counseling point is most important?

A 63-year-old woman whose hypotension was relieved by pericardiocentesis for a malignant effusion asks about her outlook. Which statement best describes her prognosis?

A 66-year-old woman in torsades de pointes (a polymorphic rhythm whose QRS complexes twist around the baseline) becomes unresponsive with a blood pressure of 60/30 and only a faint pulse. Which is the most appropriate next step?

A 26-year-old woman had a peripherally inserted central catheter placed in her right arm two weeks ago for long-term antibiotic therapy. She reports aching and swelling of the arm. Examination shows diffuse swelling of the entire right upper arm with mild redness, and there is no palpable cord and no purulent drainage. Which is the most appropriate next step?
A 70-year-old woman with a medial ankle venous ulcer has used compression, elevation and wound care for five months and the ulcer has not healed. Which referral is most appropriate?

A 29-year-old woman has had a resting heart rate of 105 to 115 for a year. Thyroid tests, a blood count, a drug screen and an echocardiogram are normal, and she takes no medications or stimulants. Her electrocardiogram shows a normal P wave before every narrow QRS. Which is the most likely diagnosis?

A 33-year-old woman eight weeks postpartum has mild calf aching and a low pretest probability of deep vein thrombosis. Her clinician orders a D-dimer. Which characteristic makes a negative result useful for excluding a clot?

A 65-year-old woman developed chest pain and dyspnea during a hurricane evacuation. She has ST elevation, an elevated troponin and B-type natriuretic peptide, and an echocardiogram showing akinesis of the left ventricular apex. Which test confirms stress cardiomyopathy?

A 70-year-old smoker has a painful, dry, punched-out ulcer at the tip of his second toe with minimal bleeding and surrounding black necrotic tissue. It started as a minor scrape months ago. Which complication is he at risk of?

An 81-year-old man with 3 months of weight loss presents with dyspnea and a large pericardial effusion. He has had no recent viral illness, chest surgery or radiation. Which etiology should be most strongly suspected?
In tachy-brady syndrome, which tachyarrhythmia is most common?

A 60-year-old woman with confirmed constrictive pericarditis has failed a 3-month trial of anti-inflammatories and diuretics and remains fluid overloaded. Which service performs the definitive procedure she needs?

A 33-year-old man has a regular narrow complex tachycardia at 190 with hidden P waves. He is alert with a blood pressure of 128/80. A properly performed vagal maneuver does not change the rhythm. Which is the next step?

A 20-year-old man has just been diagnosed with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy on echocardiography. He has two younger sisters and a brother. His mother had unexplained sudden death at 44. Which step for his family is most appropriate?

A 64-year-old man is admitted with an inferior myocardial infarction. His heart rate falls to 46 with narrow QRS complexes and P waves that are either inverted (retrograde P waves) or buried in the QRS. Which rhythm is most likely?

A 61-year-old woman with heart failure has palpitations. A 48-hour monitor shows several runs of 4 to 8 identical wide QRS beats, each lasting a few seconds, without hemodynamic compromise. Which is the first-line drug?
A 46-year-old man with frothy urine and leg swelling is found to have a moderate pericardial effusion. Which tests best evaluate the suspected cause?

A 72-year-old man with extensive atherosclerosis develops painful, tender, bluish discoloration of several toes on his left foot, with localized pallor. His dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses are easily palpable. Which is the most likely diagnosis?

A 49-year-old man has had a peripheral intravenous catheter in his right forearm for six days. He now has a fever of 39.2 degrees Celsius, a tender cord along the vein, purulent drainage at the insertion site, and redness that extends several centimeters beyond the vein margin. Which is the most likely diagnosis?
A 60-year-old woman with a prosthetic valve and a past episode of anaphylaxis to penicillin needs a dental cleaning and can take pills. Which prophylactic agent should be avoided?
A 60-year-old man who smokes has a 4.3 cm asymptomatic thoracic aortic aneurysm and a blood pressure of 158/94. He asks what he can do to help himself. Which counseling point is most appropriate?

A perivalvular abscess that extends into the epicardium causes which complication?

A 72-year-old woman has sudden chest pain and diaphoresis an hour after learning she has lost her savings in a financial collapse. The electrocardiogram shows ST elevation and troponin is elevated. No catheterization has been done yet. Which is the most appropriate initial approach?

A 58-year-old woman has a slow sinus rhythm at 38 six hours after an inferior myocardial infarction. She feels faint and her blood pressure is 80/50. Each narrow QRS has a normal P wave before it. Which drug should be given first?

A 72-year-old woman has 6 weeks of aching and stiffness in her shoulders and hips, fatigue and a low-grade fever. Her erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein are high, but no murmur is heard and three sets of blood cultures are negative. Which is the most likely diagnosis?

A 61-year-old woman with long-standing diabetes describes a continuous burning sensation in both feet that is the same at rest and during exercise. Her pedal pulses are easily palpable. Which is the most likely diagnosis?
A 70-year-old woman with atrial fibrillation at 150 has crackles throughout both lungs from pulmonary edema and a blood pressure of 82/50. Which feature makes this presentation a medical emergency?

A 67-year-old woman with hypertension has an acute aortic dissection with severe tearing chest pain and a blood pressure of 176/100. Which intravenous medication should be started first to lower her pressure?

A 59-year-old man with obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy has just undergone alcohol septal ablation, in which alcohol is injected through a catheter into a septal branch of the coronary artery. He asks when he can expect his symptoms to improve. Which answer is most accurate?
A 55-year-old man has 3 days of fever to 40.0 °C (104.0 °F), rigors and a new murmur, and he looks toxic. Which organism is a classic cause of this tempo of infective endocarditis?

An 80-year-old man has an incidental finding on a preoperative electrocardiogram: a constant PR interval in conducted beats with occasional P waves that are not followed by a QRS complex, and no PR lengthening before the dropped beats. He has no symptoms. Which is the most appropriate next step?

A 59-year-old man in ventricular fibrillation arrest is shocked several times, and his rhythm changes to a flat line with no electrical activity in two leads. What does this change mean for his outlook?

A 29-year-old woman who delivered a healthy baby three months ago now has breathlessness on exertion, orthopnea (breathlessness lying flat) and swollen ankles. She had no heart disease before pregnancy. Echocardiogram shows a dilated left ventricle with an ejection fraction of 30%. Which is the most likely diagnosis?

An 80-year-old man is found on the floor two days after collapsing. His right leg has profound sensory loss, paralysis with rigid muscles, and no arterial or venous Doppler signal. Which is the most appropriate next step?

A 58-year-old woman has Wenckebach block (a PR interval that grows longer until a beat is dropped) found on a routine tracing. She feels well and asks what would make her a candidate for a pacemaker. Which answer is most accurate?
Which laboratory finding counts as an immunologic phenomenon among the minor modified Duke criteria?

A 32-year-old woman who is 34 weeks pregnant sits in a car for nine hours and develops left calf swelling and pain. Her pregnancy supplies a hypercoagulable state and the long ride supplies venous stasis. Which additional component would complete the Virchow triad?
How is hemodynamically stable atrial flutter treated first?

A 24-year-old man whose Wolff-Parkinson-White was found on a school electrocardiogram presents with palpitations. The rhythm is irregular and wide-complex, at rates up to 260, with varying delta waves (slurred upstrokes). He is alert with a blood pressure of 118/74. Which drug is the most appropriate treatment?
A 68-year-old man has had 6 weeks of low-grade fever and weight loss and has a new murmur. Subacute endocarditis is suspected. Which complete blood count finding is most likely?

A 31-year-old man was treated for acute pericarditis 3 months ago and has been symptom-free for 6 weeks. His sharp, positional chest pain has now returned with a friction rub (a scratchy, squeaking sound). C-reactive protein is mildly raised. Which regimen is most appropriate?
